title: Lug quality: golden rule standard + improve-before-notify workflow
body:
Two related rules that should be codified in lug authoring protocol and the improve skill.

## Rule 1: Lug Quality Standard — The Golden Rule
Write a lug as if you are the next agent who will read it cold, with no session context, no memory of the conversation, and no way to ask questions. Ask: 'Would I be able to reconstruct the full situation, rationale, and intent from this lug alone?' If no, it is not done. This means:
- Body explains the full context, not just the conclusion
- Rationale is explicit: why this decision, not just what was decided
- Scope is clear: what this does AND what it does not do
- Related lugs, files, or signals are referenced by id
- No terse one-liners presented as complete entries
The bar is: another agent, another session, another model — zero prior context — must be able to act correctly from this lug alone.

## Rule 2: Improve-Before-Notify Workflow
Current behavior: write lug → tell user. Required behavior: write lug → run improve skill → THEN notify user. The improve skill is not optional post-processing — it is part of lug creation. The user should only ever see lugs that have already passed through improve. The notification to the user is the signal that the lug is complete, not that it was written.

## Why Both Together
The golden rule sets the intent; the improve workflow enforces it mechanically. Neither alone is sufficient. The improve skill running on a terse lug will catch the gap. The golden rule framing tells the agent why the gap matters.
